Due to anatomy, I get cases where a vertical preparation (verti-prep or
also called BOPT) is optimal.  These are, I know, not always candidates
for scanning but it can be done.

You may not be comfortable with this and if so, just tell me--

in the case where a vertical prep is performed and scanned:

  You, as tech, gets to decide the margin.  It's not as impossible as it
might seem.

1) Approximately a .3 mm margin with 45 degree emergence angle and
profile is the goal.
2) Mark a line at the tissue level.
3) Then mark a line below that down into the sulcus 1 to 2 mm, it's more
or less give or take, it's not exacting which I know makes dental techs
unsettled.

Place the margin line at the outermost edge of the prepared surface
where prepared tooth structure is visible in the scan.
  Avoid guessing a chamfer; do not convert the margin into an artificial
shoulder.

The final margin is to be placed subgingivally, following the scalloping
of the free gingival margin.

the soft tissue sulcus on the working model
